doc.title: Henry Johnson interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 30, 1995

title: Society big band and clarinet in the Memphis school band
summary: He played with Morris Allen's society big band, and earlier clarinet in junior high band under a jazz-pianist teacher.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: never missed a piano player at that time. But later on when I started, after that I was working with a big band that worked all of the society functions, Morris Allen, who still has a big band now today, and through that I started really getting, I always liked big band music, and when I was in Memphis I also played clarinet. Because I wanted to play trumpet but they didn’t have a trumpet then so the only thing they had left was the clarinet so I played the clarinet so I could be in the band, in the junior high school band. And I got introduced to classical music. But our band teacher was a jazz piano player around Memphis. So he always was in his office playing standards on the lunch hour. So it’s really funny how all the things work out. Now he ended up being the head of the University of Nevada. I finally searched him out and found where he was about five years ago. And so I’ve kept up with him since then.
